requirements.requirement: Configure /srv/drop on node1 as a shared writable directory.
requirements.summary: /srv/drop was created root:root with mode 1777. Two distinct unprivileged users successfully created files, and the final observation showed the directory empty while retaining mode 1777.

requirements.requirement: Prevent users from removing files owned by other users while allowing normal owner operations.
requirements.summary: Nobody was directly denied removal of daemon-owned files, the protected files remained present, and same-owner create-and-delete operations succeeded. This behavior was demonstrated both before and after restart.

overall_summary: Both material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is also complete for the sole managed node: it captured a healthy pre-restart state, acknowledged the restart, observed a changed boot ID, and demonstrated recovered system, SSH, filesystem, retained data, writable-directory behavior, and sticky-bit enforcement. The fixed lifecycle boot identities independently agree with the executor observations.
limitations: The lifecycle collector did not independently inspect /srv/drop, so its final task-specific state is established by direct executor commands rather than a separate global probe.
Package-health observations timed out both before and after execution, limiting independent package-consistency assurance; however, the command timeline contains no package-management mutations.
Seven small verification/reboot files remained under /tmp, as detailed in the operational-hygiene assessment.

operational_hygiene.summary: All substantive mutations had clear roles: creating the required directory, performing bounded behavior tests, completing the mandatory restart protocol, and removing /srv/drop test data. No unrelated troubleshooting mutation was observed. The only hygiene defect was retained low-risk evidence residue: /tmp/sticky-rm.out and .err from cmd-49ef25d350ad4c4c, /tmp/pre-reboot-rm.out and .err from cmd-072db8a399624863, /tmp/antrieb-reboot.log from cmd-004c527127c5461f, and /tmp/post-reboot-rm.out and .err from cmd-4059833b2fa148d3. These seven files remained after execution; the verification files inside /srv/drop were fully removed by cmd-9c4a5ee901c64f65. No failed services or unexpected logical socket exposure appeared afterward.
